chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Yazeed al-Kunasi, who said:

A man from our companions married a woman. He said to me, 'I would like you to ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and say to him: A man from our companions married a woman, and he claims that he used to play with her mother and kiss her, without having had sexual intercourse with her.' So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'He has lied. Tell him to separate from her.' He said, 'So I returned from my journey and informed the man of what Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) had said. By Allah, he did not refute that from himself, and he divorced her.'

key_terms.أَفْضَى إِلَيْهَا: He had intercourse with her / reached her
key_terms.فَلْيُفَارِقْهَا: Let him separate from her (divorce her)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a woman after having relations with her mother?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'istidlal' (inference) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam (peace be upon him) deduces actual consummation from the man's modest claim of 'playing' (mula'abah), thereby invalidating the marriage due to the specific prohibition of marrying a woman after having relations with her mother. The narrative highlights the scholarly emphasis on verifying claims of intimacy in cases of 'khil' al-zawjayn' (intermediate relations), where the status of the mother-daughter pair is linked. The man's immediate compliance underscores the authority of the Imam's ruling in resolving familial marital disputes.
